title: Memory weave: investigate cudaMallocAsync stalls and KV-cache compaction
creator: Maya Chen
description: We are seeing recurring GPU memory residency spikes and long tail allocation stalls under steady continuous-batching load when the KV cache is warm. Symptoms differ from classical fragmentation: memory accounting on the CUDA mempool shows many short-lived resident pages that never return to the pool fast enough, and peak resident set increases with mixed-batch-size traffic. Hypothesis: interleaving KV prefetch/free patterns with cudaMallocAsync deferred frees plus our multi-arena pooling policy is creating ephemeral cross-arena dependencies that prevent timely coalescing. This ticket collects reproducer artifacts, narrows the allocator timeline, and proposes mitigations (short-term mitigations to keep Dedicated customers stable and a medium-term allocator strategy).
comments: 2026-03-08 Carlos: Initial report from production: 3 Dedicated clusters reported 10-15% higher OOM/rescheduling during 99th percentile load. Attached GPU resident graphs and a flame chart collected via nvprof wrapper.

2026-03-09 Maya: Reproducer created on dev rig: 4-GPU A100 node, steady 120 RPS, mixed sequence lengths (mean 256, tail 2048), KV cache hit rate ~72%. Reproducer reliably triggers a 2.3 GB unexplained resident increase after 20 minutes.

2026-03-10 Carlos: Heap snapshots (mempool counters) show many arenas reporting 'stalled' deferred_free queues. Instrumented tracepoints added in allocator to log allocation origin, stream id, batch id, and kv-entry id — logs captured in /tmp/mem-weave-trace-20260310.log and uploaded to the investigation Confluence page.

2026-03-11 Carlos: Experiment: forcing immediate cudaFree path (disable cudaMallocAsync) reduces peak resident by ~30% but increases P50 latency by 6ms and token throughput drops under mixed batches. Trade-off documented and benchmarked in runtime-allocator/bench PR (#1234).

2026-03-12 Maya: Ran focused test with KV prefetch disabled for 30 minutes. Resident growth stopped but end-to-end token cost increased due to more cache misses. Suggests interplay between aggressive prefetch and deferred frees as root contributor.

2026-03-12 Carlos: Opened draft PR to add an arena quarantine pass: when deferred_free queue length for an arena exceeds threshold, trigger a synchronous drain on that arena only and force free on that CUDA stream. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1278

2026-03-13 Maya: Noted regression risk: synchronous draining increases tail latency for the specific request that triggers it. Proposed mitigation: only enable synchronous drain when memory headroom < 8% and for low-priority background batches.

2026-03-13 Carlos: Next steps: (1) Add controlled rollout flag behind runtime-config for quarantine drain; (2) Add allocator telemetry for deferred_free queue length to console dashboards (dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.net/d/alloc/kv-quarantine); (3) Validate reduced-residency path on staging with 48hr soak.
